title: The Arrival of COVID-19 (2020)
text: COVID-19 was first identified in Wuhan in December 2019. However, it did not reach Mexico until February 2020, when it quickly spread across the country. During the first months of the pandemic, public health restrictions were introduced as the number of reported cases increased steadily. The year concluded with the beginning of the national vaccination campaign.

annotations.text: National vaccination campaign begins amid rising cases

title: Successive Waves and Mass Vaccination (2021)
text: Throughout 2021, Mexico experienced multiple waves of infections, including a large surge at the beginning of the year followed by another wave driven by the Delta variant. At the same time, the vaccination campaign expanded rapidly, becoming one of the country’s main public health strategies.

annotations.text: Third wave driven by the Delta variant

title: Omicron and the Transition to Recovery (2022)
text: The highly transmissible Omicron variant produced the largest surge in reported cases at the beginning of the year. Despite additional waves, vaccination helped reduce severe outcomes, and the country gradually transitioned toward normal social and economic activities.

annotations.text: Fifth wave associated with Omicron subvariants

title: The End of the Public Health Emergency (2023)
text: By 2023, reported cases had declined considerably compared with previous years. Although COVID-19 continued to circulate, the pandemic entered a new stage marked by lower transmission and the end of the global public health emergency.

annotations.text: Sixth wave with milder disease severity
